messages:
Leila: quick heads up — I ran a perf sweep on the mixed-precision rollout and hit an odd p99 regression when AUTO quant picks INT8 kernels for some decoder layers. Not sure if it's kernel selection or batching/KV interaction. Posting profiling + thoughts.

Ashwin: can you paste numbers and repro?

Leila: baseline fp16 p50=52ms p99=180ms, int8-auto p50=44ms p99=230ms — so tail got worse even though median improved. KV cache hit ratio drops ~5% in chat workloads. Repro: small prompt (2 tokens), then streaming 512-token generation across many concurrent short-turn chats.

Sam: hmm sounds like kernel choice + batching heuristics causing cache churn or micro-batch fallbacks. INT8 may be faster per-op but causes more partial-exec fallback paths for small seqs.

Marta: do we have calibration logs? If quant calibration fails it might fall back to reference kernels and blow up p99.

Leila: pasted the profiler snippet (truncated):
```
[profiler] model: redwood-4b-mix
seq=8->512 | kernel=fp8_gemm | time_per_token=0.42ms
seq=8->512 | kernel=int8_gemm | time_per_token=0.31ms
kv-cache-miss-rate: 0.07 -> 0.12
fallbacks: 4 (quant calibration warnings)
```

Ashwin: yep — see the `fallbacks` line. Those layers hit calibration tolerance and runtime switched to reference kernels for those micro-batches, producing tail spikes. We should expose a small set of calibration/fallback knobs in the SDK so teams can control safety vs speed: e.g. `calibration_safety: strict|lenient|auto` and `fallback_policy: soft|hard`.

Sam: naming proposal for the SDK config surface (minimal): `quant.mode` ("auto" | "manual"), `quant.preset` ("fast", "balanced", "robust"), `quant.calibrate_on_start` (bool), `quant.calibration_safety` ("strict", "warn", "off"). Example payload: 
```
{
  "quant.mode": "auto",
  "quant.preset": "balanced",
  "quant.calibrate_on_start": true,
  "quant.calibration_safety": "warn"
}
```

Marta: docs guidance idea: default to "balanced". Recommend "robust" for conversational workloads with many short increments and where p99 matters. Also call out `kv_prefetch=true` as a compatibility tweak when using low-bit kernels to reduce cache-miss-driven tail latency.

ci-bot: perf-alert: regression detected on pr #9123 — p99 increased 28% for small-seq chat scenario. Link: https://ci.example/9123

Leila: proposed action items:
1) Add the SDK knobs (typed enums + safe defaults).
2) Emit telemetry events for calibration warnings + exact layer ids that fallback.
3) Docs: add presets table, recipe for "chat" workloads, and explicit safety-state guidance.
4) Rollback kernel-selection change behind feature flag for the next rollout until we have better heuristics.

Sam: I'll draft the SDK change and a short compatibility test.
Ashwin: filing an instrumentation issue to log per-layer fallback reasons and quant-range histograms.
Marta: I'll draft the docs recipe and add the `kv_prefetch` note to the quickstart.

Leila: thanks — will add a changelog note for Dedicated customers about the default switching behavior and the new knobs. :thumbsup:

Sam: one more thought — add a runtime flag `prefer_stable_p99=true` that forces kernel choices to bias toward less p99 variance. Could be useful for enterprise SLAs.

Ashwin: good idea, add to the SDK wishlist.

Leila: ok closing here, follow ups as issues + docs PRs.
